note: Where US households' money goes in 2025, in the notebook's seven categories. Items are BEA PCE lines (US residents, nonresidents' spending removed) and sum to PCE exactly; saving items sum to NIPA personal saving. Interest on consumer debt and transfers paid are outside PCE (outsidePce on jeopardy and collective) but inside the history shares, so the seven history shares of disposable income sum to 1. Item industry weights are the domestic value added captured along the supply chain per dollar (BEA 2024 Use table, Leontief, research/flows.json), renormalized over the 25 industry ids; importShare is the leak abroad per dollar (direct and indirect imports). PCE 2025 = $20954.9B in both NIPA 2.4.5U and 2.6 (consistent with personal outlays $21819.4B = PCE + interest $577.7B + transfers $286.8B); the Q4-2025 SAAR ($21,363B) and the Sept-2026 annual update are not used.

totals.note: Nonresidents' spending in the US (BEA line 338, $208.9B in 2025) is subtracted from the items visitors buy (college tuition and housing for foreign students; hotels, restaurants, shopping, recreation and local transport for tourists, using an approximate visitor-spending mix), so items are US residents' spending and sum to PCE. Goods are split at purchaser prices into producer, trade and freight margins; recalled margin shapes by kind of good are scaled by tradeMarginScale so all goods margins equal the trade sector's PCE in the 2024 Use table ($3,189B of $6,262B goods, grown to 2025).

categories.name: Necessities
categories.blurb: Food at home, a basic home, utilities, getting to work, basic clothes and a phone: the floor every household pays for first.
categories.note: Design defaults kept (x 0, y 0.45, z 0.35; fearShare 0.5: as much fleeing hunger and cold as wanting food and a home). Basic level = CE 2024 second-quintile mean as a share of the all-unit mean (shelter 0.729, vehicles 0.548, apparel 0.664, furnishings 0.580); the rest of those lines is status. Desire/fear weights follow the money: shelter and utilities are about half, food a third. Owners' imputed rent ($1,823B of this category) is a BEA imputation, not a cash outlay. Category fantasy = spending-weighted mean of item fantasy (judgment: 0 buys the function, 1 buys the story).

categories.blurb: Alcohol, tobacco, gambling losses, screens, games, shows and pets: paying to feel good now or to stop feeling bad.
categories.note: fearShare 0.15 (x -0.7) instead of the design's -0.8: escape is partly flight from stress and loneliness (coping motives; negative reinforcement when relieving stress, research/psychology.json), so isolation carries most of the fear weight. Illicit drugs (~$146B, RAND 2016) and most legal cannabis are outside PCE and appear only in markets. Gambling is net losses (wagers less prizes), not handle. Attention sold to advertisers (US internet ads $295B) is paid by firms, not households, and is a market label only. outsidePce.name: Interest on consumer debt (cards, auto, student)
outsidePce.note: BEA personal interest payments (non-mortgage), NIPA 2.6, 2025. Routed to banking (banks, card issuers, auto lenders) and finance (student-loan and other nonbank lenders): approximate split. Mortgage interest (~$505B) is inside owners' imputed rent in BEA accounting.

categories.blurb: Doctors, hospitals, drugs, insurance, lawyers, bank charges and interest on debt: paying to escape a threat.
categories.note: fearShare 0.85 (x 0.7, design 0.8): mostly fear of illness, loss and ruin, but some care is wanted (elective, preventive) and life insurance protects others. y 0.4 and z 0.3 (design 0.35, 0.25) because $1.0T of the category is deliberate, future-facing asset fees. Health care is counted with all payers (insurers, Medicare, Medicaid), as in PCE; households pay ~$0.5T out of pocket (CMS NHE). The financial-sector charges for holding assets (implicit bank and pension services, investment management, brokerage: $1,009B, items flagged assetFee) are PCE, not saving, so they sit here on the notebook's Services -> Jeopardy line; a view can move them next to saving. Interest on consumer debt is outside PCE (outsidePce) but inside the history share. Category fantasy = spending-weighted mean of item fantasy (judgment: 0 buys the function, 1 buys the story).

categories.name: Collective

outsidePce.name: Transfers paid: remittances abroad, fees & fines
outsidePce.note: BEA personal current transfer payments, NIPA 2.6, 2025: to government (fees, fines, donations) and to the rest of the world (net remittances). The government/abroad split is not in the research data; weights are a placeholder (the remittance part leaves the country).

categories.blurb: Congregations, charities, unions, civic groups and gifts beyond the household: money spent on the group.
categories.note: Design defaults kept (x 0.1, y 0.6, z 0.6). Mostly the final consumption of nonprofits serving households ($608B, BEA): what churches, charities, nonprofit schools and hospitals spend beyond what they sell, funded by giving. Personal transfer payments (to government: fees, fines; to the rest of the world: remittances, net) are outside PCE (outsidePce) but inside the history share. Individual giving was ~$392B in 2024 (Giving USA, recalled). Category fantasy = spending-weighted mean of item fantasy (judgment: 0 buys the function, 1 buys the story).

items.name: Congregations (nonprofit spending)
items.note: NPISH final consumption: gross output less sales to households, funded by donations, dues and grants.

categories.name: Saving & trading assets
categories.blurb: Net saving into pensions, home equity, stocks, deposits, a business and speculation: buying the future.
categories.note: Design defaults kept (x 0.2, y 0.8, z 0.95): saving is mostly fear of a poor old age and loss of the home, with desire for a house and rank. Items split NIPA personal saving 2025 ($1046.8B) into rough uses: each income quintile's 2024 saving (BEA distribution of personal saving: the bottom 40% dissave, the top 20% does ~80% of net saving) is assumed to flow into its assets in proportion to its DFA 2026Q1 holdings (net of matching debts, excluding durables). Crypto is a recalled anchor (low confidence). Industry weights here route the money to intermediaries (banks, funds, insurers, builders), they are not value added; the business item uses the investment supply chain. Fees for holding assets are PCE and sit in jeopardy. Category fantasy = spending-weighted mean of item fantasy (judgment: 0 buys the function, 1 buys the story).

items.name: Retirement accounts & pensions
items.note: DB and DC pension entitlements, life insurance and annuities. Routed to finance (pension funds, asset managers) and insurance by DFA holdings.

items.name: Home equity: mortgage principal & improvements
items.note: Owner-occupied real estate net of mortgages. Split between lenders (principal repaid, CE 2024 $397B) and builders (home improvements, CE 2024 $353B).

items.name: Stocks & mutual funds
items.note: Corporate equities and mutual funds held directly (crypto ETF buying carved out below).

items.name: Deposits, money funds & bonds
items.note: Bank deposits (banking) and money-market funds, bonds and other financial assets (finance), net of consumer credit.

items.name: Crypto & speculation
items.note: Recalled anchor, low confidence: US spot bitcoin and ether ETF net inflows in 2025 were roughly $31B (Farside/Bloomberg tallies); used as the order of magnitude of households' net crypto buying. Direct exchange buying is not measured.

historyNote: Shares of disposable personal income, 1950-2026 (2026 = Jan-Jul SAAR). Saving = personal saving / DPI. The other six: each BEA major type of PCE (Tables 2.3.5/2.8.5) is split into categories with its 2025 split from the items (historyMapping), so the 2025 row reproduces the items exactly; interest paid (non-mortgage) is added to jeopardy and transfers paid (DPI - PCE - interest - saving) to collective. Before 1959 BEA has only total services; it is split with the 1959 service mix. BEA books the nonresident deduction in other services, so that type carries a small negative escapism weight. Within-type mixes are held at 2025 values, so shifts inside a type (e.g. more gambling within recreation) are not captured. 1950-1987 come from an older BEA vintage than 1988-2026.
byQuintileNote: BLS CE 2024, quintiles of income before taxes (27.1-27.3M consumer units each). incomeMean = CE income after taxes less estimated Social Security/Medicare payroll deductions (CE all-unit $6684 spread by wages + 2 x self-employment income), the NIPA disposable-income concept. spendingMean = CE spending excluding pensions and Social Security. shares = category spending / incomeMean, with saving = 1 - spending / income (retirement contributions count as saving); negative for the bottom 40%: CE under-reports income at the bottom, and many there are retirees and students drawing on assets or family. Category rules follow research (ceSurvey2024ModelCategoriesByQuintile): basic level = second-quintile mean; status = food away, shelter above basic, travel; jeopardy includes household-paid health premiums, vehicle finance charges and insurance. The survey misses most vice spending (alcohol ~22% of PCE, tobacco ~41%, lottery ~8%, casino losses ~0%) and third-party health care and imputed rent, so ceToPce gives national PCE items / (CE mean x units) per category, and pceBasisShares rescales each quintile's CE categories by it (shares of spending, PCE basis).
